question.text: What are the consequences for a trading member who violates position limits in derivative trading?

answer.text: The exchange/CC monitors position limits and imposes penalties for violations — the member may be required to reduce positions within prescribed time; persistent violations can lead to suspension of trading rights
There are no penalties for position limit violations as they are only advisory limits
The member is permanently banned from trading on all exchanges
Only a warning letter is issued with no financial penalty

explanation.text: The Logic: Position limits are monitored by exchanges and clearing corporations. A violator cannot take fresh positions and must reduce or close out positions to bring exposures within the permitted limits. Penalties may be levied, and the clearing corporation/exchange may withdraw trading or clearing facilities and close out positions. The Trap: Position limits are mandatory, not advisory; consequences are not limited to warning letters; and permanent bans across all exchanges are not the standard response. Note: Position-limit enforcement applies across derivative segments; the specific monitoring and action sequence follows the relevant exchange and clearing corporation rules.
